## Proposed change
Bump Haanna to 0.14.0, fixing the reported Home Assistant issues:
#28815
#28947
#30714
and the error reported in haanna issue #14.
Also, the proposed fix for the issue reported by fwestenberg, related to 2 Annas in one HA system, is included.

Update to climate.py, fixing:
#28947: add detection of the heating_state for on/off-type heaters via the boiler_state parameter.

issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
- If you need additional help with this template please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
- Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/releases
- Frontend issues should be submitted to the home-assistant-polymer repository: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant-polymer/issues
- iOS issues should be submitted to the home-assistant-iOS repository: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant-iOS/issues
- Android issues should be submitted to the home-assistant-android repository: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant-android/issues
- Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom integration: files in <config-dir>/custom_components
- This is for bugs only. Feature and enhancement requests should go in our community forum: https://community.home-assistant.io/c/feature-requests
- Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration sample and code into the backticks. Do not delete any text from this template!
-->

**Home Assistant release with the issue:** 0.103.6
<!--
- Frontend -> Developer tools -> Info
- Or use this command: hass --version
-->


**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**


**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):** Linux (Raspbian Buster Lite) venv install
<!--
Please provide details about your environment.
-->

**Integration:** Plugwise
<!--
Please add the link to the documentation at https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/ of the integration in question.
-->


**Description of problem:** I have a legacy Anna. When enabling the component and starting hass, an error is produced:
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.climate] plugwise: Error on device update!



**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**
```yaml
climate:
  - platform: plugwise
    password: <smileID>
    host: <hostname>
    legacy_anna: true

```

**Traceback (if applicable):**
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 292, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.async_device_update(warning=False)
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 461, in async_device_update
    await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(self.update)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 57, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/homeassistant/components/plugwise/climate.py", line 262, in update
    self._domain_objects = self._api.get_domain_objects()
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/haanna/haanna.py", line 67, in get_domain_objects
    return Etree.fromstring(r.text)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/xml/etree/ElementTree.py", line 1315, in XML
    parser.feed(text)
  File "<string>", line None
xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 216, column 42
```

**Additional information:** When getting the URL manually (and verifying it with a tcpdump from the Pi), it seems that this line (216) is the culprit:
		<vendor_name>Viessmann Elektronik GmbH & Co KG</vendor_name>
Something wrong the way the ampersand is encoded?
comments: Yes. Ampersand is special in xml. It must be written as &
If you can't get the manufacturer to fix. Upstream library must try to handle the invalid XML.

i created a support case with Plugwise too... but i think they aren't gonna fix it anytime soon.

Maybe i'll just do a string replace before passing it to the parser...

Hey there @laetificat, @CoMPaTech, @bouwew, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`plugwise`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L261) for? Thanks!
If the update from the post above does not work, I think I have found a solution that should work. It works in my simple simulation-environment.

Seems like the dev custom component change isn't working:

`2020-01-13 17:27:17 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.climate] plugwise_dev: Error on device update!`
...
`xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 216, column 42`

Ok, noted. Please change the haanna version to 0.14.2 in manifest.json, then restart HA.
Let me know the result, please.

Nice! Thanks for testing.
I will push all the latest updates into HA, once I have received the confirmation from several other users that all is working OK.
So when that's done i can revert back to the original integration i guess...

@oxje We are working on a common platform for all Plugwise devices. There will be support for the Plugwise Anna's, Smile P1's and the Adam, and Plugs via the Adam. We have tested with the Adam, Plugs and the Anna with firmware 3.1.11. Now we are looking for testers that have a legacy Anna. Are you willing to help?

review_comments: If the item value is unknown or missing we don't add the item at all to state attributes.

Update2, when no schedule is active, the haanna-code looks for the last active schedule and outputs that into the `selected_schema` attribute. That is not a great solution I realise now. I'll try to fix this via another haanna update and some changes to the climate.py-code.

Update, never mind, I understand what you mean.
I removed the `else'-part and now I've found a bug...

The STATES shows this:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11290930/73124504-675fc880-3f9c-11ea-976d-262a9b31df59.png)
The code is written like that to show that no schedule is selected, shown by the value 'None'.
Without the added code, it would show 'null', which I find unacceptable.
From python perspective it would make sense, but for user experience it provides a clear 'you didn't create any schedules' indication.
We shouldn't add the key either in the state attributes if the value is not set. So the item will not show at all.
If the item value is unknown or missing we don't add the item at all to state attributes.
